relevance_note: Single case report of a GFAP variant carrier: "Whole-exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous missense variant in exon 6 of GFAP".
method_note: Read by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. No tables in the paper; no supplementary text available (supplement headings only). Individuals: the proband ('patient', single unnamed case-report patient), relatives described in relation to him (youngest brother, tested carrier; mother, tested negative; late father with dementing illness; paternal uncle and late paternal aunt with cerebellar ataxia, none of the last three tested), and two previously published carriers of the same variant described with age, sex and features in the Discussion (refs [6] and [13]). Not given rows: the middle of the '3 male siblings' (no facts given); the 'four adults from the same kindred' carrying the complex allele c.988C>G; p.(Arg330)Gly-c.G994A; p.(Glu332Lys) [14] (group-level only, no individual facts); the 'two subjects' with dementia [10] (no variant, group-level). Pathogenicity for the proband: the paper says it was 'defined as likely pathogenic according to the American College of Medical Genetics criteria' and also calls it 'pathogenic' (abstract; ClinVar registration; 'confirming this variant as pathogenic'); recorded the authors' ACMG classification for the proband and the general 'pathogenic' statement (which names this exact variant) for the other carriers. Functional evidence (U-251-MG transfection, ref [15]) is about this exact variant and was attached to all four carriers. Variant type and zygosity were stated only in the proband's sentence and left 'not reported' for the brother and the literature patients. Inheritance not reported: mother tested negative but father not tested, so not de novo. Age at onset of the proband is not given as an age ('during the last 2 years' before presentation at 43); recorded as onset of the laryngeal tremor feature only. Ages 61 and 57 for the literature patients were recorded as age at report; the paper does not say whether they are ages at onset or at report. Country not recorded: the paper only says AOAxD 'has not been described in the Spanish population yet'. D-27: 'normal neurological examinations' in mother and brother recorded as excluded 'abnormal neurological examination' only; no specific checklist item excluded. 'Other neurologic symptoms' denied by the proband excludes nothing specific. 'Periventricular rim' left not reported: the paper describes periventricular white matter hyperintensity, not a rim. Contradiction-like wording: the conclusion says palatal tremor 'has not been reported' for this variant (refers to earlier reports) while describing palatopharyngeal tremor in this patient.
